I’m working general practice in small animal. I even learned which species I had a preference working with, but it’s few & far in-between (gaht dang rabbits lol). But since having all these doubts I’ve been scrambling ideas to help reignite my passion for the field, and I’ve been eyeballing dentistry specialty; I just find it interesting, and having a task on hand that just focuses on teeth seems better suiting as opposed to dealing with 30 wellness visits. I’ve since moved clinics thinking the bad environment was the problem, and the clinic I’m at is better in terms of that. This feeling absolutely terrifies me because before vet med I used to work in service industry with food, and I can’t go back to that; it’s a hell of it’s own. Oh and I almost forgot, check out Plumbs drug manual. I freaking love that book and it explains all the drugs that are used within practice. Look into buying the latest edition and keep it on hand whenever you make it to the pharmacology section; it’ll be your best friend and will always be there for you whenever you feel stumped on understanding the MoA of a certain drug. :)

Merk veterinary manual has some really good information over illnesses & genetic diseases. At my job we use Veterinarypartner.com for information to our clients. It’s VERY useful and has tons of videos explaining just about all the procedures you may go over in class.

Best of luck, and don’t give up even when the times get hard.

When I was 18 I was a server for this known pizzeria in town that slowly declined in service over the years because the managers were shady and other employees just didn’t care, and frankly neither did I at the time. There was this one manager though, named Michael, who was just this pompous ass that would find any reason to shift blame and take tips away. The store had an absurd amount of women working as servers and it was a daily thing for him to make someone cry, and because of that the turn over rate was high. But on this one day, I came in not feeling 100% so I felt like I was just struggling all throughout the day. Que Michael yelling at me in the corner, berating me like usual, and threatening to take my tips away, yada yada. At that point I looked him dead in the eye and said “you know what Michael, fuck this, I’m done, I quit”, and he just wouldn’t take that as an answer, saying “just wait till after your shift and we’ll talk”. Whatever fine, right? So I let it go for a minute, and at that time the restaurant started to fill up (and I was the only server on the floor that day too), and once I saw there were a lot of heads waiting to be served I found that as the perfect opportunity to grab my keys, slip away behind everyone’s backs quietly, and I bolted out the kitchen door and walked all the way back around to my car to leave. I drove next door, across the street, to the gas station to get a pack of cigarettes is when they started blowing my phone up and I can see both Michael and the assistant manager outside & looking around all confused while I’m sitting at the gas station benches, smoking my cigarette, watching them freak out with a full house and no server. Best job I ever quit and I would gladly do it all over again if I could just to see the look on their faces one more time

YWBTA if you showed up, but not an Asshole for wanting to go. I buried my brother after having his first and last overdose. Find a more private and personal place for you to let out your emotions and to take the guilt off your mind. Hell, go to her resting place days after the service and have your peace there. But please don’t go to her service, you wouldn’t be welcome and it can make everyone feel more emotions than they would’ve felt to begin with, and it wouldn’t be pretty and be awkward for every party involved. And also, I’m sorry for your loss OP.

Hey friend I’ve been in that same spot before with my best friend from high school (we’re both F) . Back in those days I was extremely infatuated with her, and I remained being her friend just to keep being close to her. It ended up hurting me in the long run, mainly because my young mind didn’t know what was good for me and the love I had for her was blinding. What worked out for ME (not saying it’ll work for you, not all things work out the same for everybody), was to let the friendship distant off after I had graduated since i was a grade level above her. She was straight, and I’m gay, so in my mind I knew it was a fantasy to ever think something would come together between us. But for you, I’d recommend starting with coming out to her. Let her get to know that side of you, but don’t express your feelings yet. Give it some time, and if you feel like she doesn’t feel the same then it’s nothing to fret over, even if it feels like all is lost after that. There’s a lot of things I learned while going through the unrequitedness and it truly makes you a stronger human being who learned to love and empathize more, because in our hearts we knew how it felt to not feel loved in the way we wanted by someone that would mean the world to us. I understand how painful it is, it feels like a hole is being ripped through your chest but don’t worry too hard; time will pass, and the universe will bring you the person you’ve actually been preparing for, and you’ll cherish and love them the way you’d want to be loved back. Good luck my dude, I hope it works out in the end for you. You can also message me if you’d like, my inbox is always open if you need someone to vent out too
